claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a yield strength of approximately 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
Rapid solidification followed by controlled homogenization will produce a refined dendritic microstructure.
The resulting microstructure will contain a continuous, percolating Ti/Zr-enriched matrix.
The resulting microstructure will contain refractory-rich interdendritic regions.
Cooling rates above 10^5 K/s restrict elemental diffusion.
Restricted diffusion during rapid solidification promotes microsegregation of Ti and Zr into a percolating matrix.
Accumulation of lighter Ti and Zr in the matrix will reduce the alloy's overall density.
Post-solidification homogenization will create a controlled and uniform distribution of the segregated microstructural features.
Refractory-rich interdendritic regions will provide solid-solution strengthening.
The proposed microstructure will provide grain-boundary strengthening.
The refractory-rich regions will preserve yield strength at room temperature and 1000 °C.
The intervention will reduce density by approximately 10–15% relative to the as-cast alloy.
The processed alloy will retain room-temperature yield strength within 10% of approximately 1600 MPa.
The processed alloy will have a yield strength of approximately 850 MPa at 1000 °C.
The processed alloy will retain tensile ductility above 40%.
Mechanical performance will be evaluated by quasi-static tensile testing at room temperature and 1000 °C.
The processed samples and baseline will be tested using identical loading rates.

contradictions.description: The intervention only redistributes elements within an unchanged HfMoTaTiZr composition, yet the mechanism attributes a 10–15% reduction in bulk density to Ti/Zr segregation. Forming a low-density region does not by itself reduce composition-averaged density without elemental removal, added porosity, or a sufficiently large volume change.

Homogenization is said to ensure a uniform elemental distribution while the required mediator is persistent Ti/Zr enrichment and refractory-rich microsegregation. The intended degree of homogenization versus segregation is not resolved.

Being within 10% of 1600 MPa permits room-temperature yield strength as low as 1440 MPa, but the experiment declares any value below 1450 MPa falsifying. Thus values from 1440 to below 1450 MPa simultaneously meet the prediction and trigger rejection.
